name: Standing Ab Wheel Rollout
description: The standing ab wheel rollout is an advanced progression of the kneeling rollout that starts with the athlete fully upright, dramatically increasing the moment arm at the shoulder and hip. The exercise demands elite levels of anti-extension core stiffness, shoulder stability, and lat engagement to prevent collapse of the lumbar spine as the wheel rolls forward. It represents one of the highest anti-extension challenges achievable with minimal equipment and should only be attempted after mastering the kneeling variation.

execution.starting_position: Stand upright holding the ab wheel handles with both hands, wheel on the floor just in front of the feet.
execution.setup_instructions: Only attempt after achieving 15+ controlled kneeling rollouts with full range of motion. Use a non-slip surface.
steps: Step 1: Brace the core maximally. Begin to roll the wheel forward while simultaneously hinging at the hips.
Step 2: Lower the torso toward the floor under strict anti-extension control — do not allow the lumbar spine to hyperextend.
Step 3: Extend forward as far as can be controlled — ideally until the body is nearly horizontal.
Step 4: Pull the wheel back toward the feet by engaging the lats and abs simultaneously, returning to upright.
Step 5: Maintain a hollow-body position throughout — ribs down, pelvis neutral.
execution.breathing_instructions: Inhale and brace before rolling out. Exhale sharply on the return.
common_mistakes: Lumbar hyperextension at the bottom — indicates insufficient core strength for this variation
Failing to engage the lats on the return — the pullback is lat-driven, not just abs
safety_considerations: Stop immediately if lower-back pain occurs — regress to kneeling rollout
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Roll out as far as can be controlled without lumbar collapse. Full return to standing upright.
execution.tempo_recommendations: 3-1-3-0. Each repetition should be fully deliberate and controlled.
coaching_cues: Ribs to hips — hollow position always
Pull the floor toward you on the way back
